consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning across responses: symbolic beasts (esp. Daniel/Revelation) represent God-opposing earthly political powers, kingdoms/empires, or rulers that persecute God's people (with identification debates: Antichrist, Rome/Nero, papacy, or timeless evil). Alternatives include base/carnal human nature, demonic forces, chaos, or (minority) Gentiles/unclean peoples; literal animals also noted. Settled at the general 'oppressive kingdom/ruler' level.
book_summary: A nation or kingdom of the world as the wild, predatory figure of a people (analogous to trees as rooted figures); different beasts are different kingdoms; unclean beasts are the Gentile nations God cleanses in Peter's vision.
consensus_core_identification: God-opposing kingdoms, empires, or rulers (brutal/idolatrous political powers).
book_core_identification: A nation or kingdom of the world (wild predatory figure of a people); unclean beasts specifically as Gentile nations.
boundary_disagreement: Book generalizes beyond consensus's primary anti-God/oppressive/apocalyptic focus to any world nation/people as predatory figure, and elevates unclean beasts (Acts 10) as Gentile nations (a minority alternative in consensus) into the core entry.
material_contradiction: None; both treat beasts as representing kingdoms/nations/peoples (explicitly via Dan 7/8), without mutual exclusion of the central category.
rationale: Minimum cores both reduce to beasts = kingdoms/nations (directly from Dan 7:17/8:20-21). Book preserves this general referent/category from consensus primary but materially broadens extension/boundaries: neutral 'of the world' (not restricted to opposing/satanic), plus predatory-people framing and unclean=Gentiles application. This is refinement of cases/precision, not core replacement or novelty (Gentiles alt appears in consensus). Citations alone match book's claims without needing full-chapter context.
strongest_objection: Consensus treats the primary apocalyptic referent as specifically oppressive/anti-God powers (with Acts 10 unclean animals as a separate minority metaphor for Gentiles, not continuous with the beast symbolism of Daniel/Revelation).
